detailed_rationale: [DATA] Havells FY26 (Apr-25-Mar-26): consolidated revenue +3.44% YoY, PAT +14.9% YoY to Rs.1,689cr (vs Rs.1,470cr FY25). Q4 FY26 (Jan-Mar26) alone: revenue +2.4% YoY to ~Rs.6,688-6,705cr, PAT +~40% YoY to Rs.723cr, but EBITDA fell 3.6% YoY with margin contracting to 10.9% from 11.6%. [DATA] Segment mix Q4 FY26: Cables +14% YoY to Rs.2,474cr (FY26 full-year cables +20.8% to Rs.8,677cr) - the clear growth engine, capex/power-T&D-cycle-led. Switchgear +6.4% to Rs.736cr but margin compressed by a lag in passing through input-cost (copper/aluminium) increases, management says normalising. ECD -2% to Rs.976cr on a milder-than-expected start to summer. Lloyd (AC/consumer) -19% YoY to Rs.1,514cr on delayed seasonality - Q3 FY26 Lloyd was already down 6.5% YoY (Rs.694cr), so Lloyd printed two consecutive soft quarters heading into peak season; the segment's known profitability drag persisted. [DATA] Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun26, reported 17-Jul-26, PIT-fresh): revenue +19% YoY to ~Rs.6,518-6,572cr, but consolidated PAT fell 16.6% YoY to Rs.289.71cr and EBITDA (ex other income) fell 9.6% YoY to Rs.466cr. Segment mix reversed the Q4 story: Cables +27% YoY (Rs.2,455.62cr, standout), Lloyd +14.6% YoY (Rs.1,457.44cr - a decent summer read though delayed onset capped full seasonal benefit), ECD +11.8% YoY (Rs.1,113.07cr), Switchgear revenue fell to Rs.607.68cr on West-Asia-linked export disruption even as domestic demand held. [INFERENCE] The Q1 FY27 profit decline is not a demand problem - it is a deliberate margin-for-share trade: consolidated A&P spend more than doubled (+100.5% YoY to Rs.286.51cr) to defend/build share against Crompton (fans/value), Voltas, and Korean/Chinese AC brands (LG, Samsung, Daikin, Blue Star premium range) amid intensifying ECD/AC competition. [DATA] ONE-OFF CHECK: Q4 FY26's ~40% PAT beat is flattered by a Rs.283cr non-operating fair-value gain on Havells' Rs.600cr Goldi Solar Pvt Ltd investment (made Q1 FY26) - strip that out and Q4 operating performance (EBITDA -3.6% YoY, margin -70bps) was soft; FY26's headline +14.9% PAT growth vs +3.44% revenue growth is partly this one-off, not a volume/mix story.
recommendation_rationale: [INFERENCE] Fundamentals are mixed, not broken: cables (the largest, highest-growth segment, +20-27% YoY across the last two prints) is genuinely strong and capex-cycle-linked, ECD is recovering (+11.8% Q1FY27), and Lloyd's Q1 FY27 print (+14.6%) shows the AC business is not structurally impaired - just volatile and onset-timing-dependent, consistent with the known monsoon/summer-season demand-cycle lens on this coverage. Switchgear softness is input-cost-lag plus a one-off West Asia export disruption, not evidence of competitive share loss. Margin compression across FY26-Q4 and Q1FY27 is explained by (a) a genuine non-operating one-off (Goldi Solar FV gain inflating the year-ago PAT comparison) and (b) a deliberate, disclosed A&P investment to defend share - a reversible strategic choice, not an earnings-quality or balance-sheet red flag. [DATA] No quant score exists yet for HAVELLS (verified: no HAVELLS row present in STOCK_SCORECARD_750/results/ as of this pass), so under V1 asymmetric-override rules there is no score-Sell to rescue, and a fresh Sell cannot be manufactured from fundamentals alone absent that trigger. [OPINION] Separately on valuation: TTM PE ~40-43x against a business whose FY26 core (ex one-off) EBITDA was flat-to-down and whose Q1FY27 core EBITDA fell 9.6% YoY is rich and priced for more than the current growth run-rate is delivering - a valuation caution, not a fundamentals-Sell trigger. Net call: Hold - a decent core franchise (cables) carrying a known-and-recovering cyclical segment (Lloyd) through deliberate (not structural) margin pressure, but a rich multiple leaves little room for further Lloyd/switchgear disappointment.
summary: Havells FY26/Q1FY27: cables the star (+20-27% YoY, capex-led), Lloyd AC volatile (Q3 FY26 -6.5%, Q4 FY26 -19% on delayed season, Q1 FY27 +14.6% on a decent-but-late summer), switchgear soft on cost-lag plus West Asia export disruption, ECD recovering. Q4 FY26's ~40% PAT beat was flattered by a Rs.283cr Goldi Solar fair-value one-off; Q1 FY27's 16.6% PAT decline is a deliberate, doubled A&P-spend margin trade to defend share vs Crompton/Voltas/Korean-Chinese AC brands, not a demand collapse. Valuation rich (~40x PE) versus core growth actually delivered. Hold.
positive_para: [DATA] Cables & wires - Havells' largest segment - grew 14% YoY in Q4 FY26 and accelerated to 27% YoY in Q1 FY27 (Rs.2,455.62cr), with FY26 full-year cables revenue up 20.8% to Rs.8,677cr; this is capex/power-T&D-cycle-linked and the clearest structural growth driver in the portfolio. [DATA] Lloyd's Q1 FY27 print (+14.6% YoY, Rs.1,457.44cr) during peak AC season shows the segment recovering off two soft prints (Q3 FY26 -6.5%, Q4 FY26 -19%) - a delayed monsoon/summer onset capped rather than killed the season. [DATA] ECD grew 11.8% YoY in Q1 FY27 after a soft Q4 FY26 (-2%), a second consecutive-quarter improvement trend. [INFERENCE] Margin compression in FY26-Q1FY27 is substantially self-inflicted (doubled A&P spend, +100.5% YoY) rather than competitive share loss or cost-structure damage - a reversible, disclosed strategic choice - and switchgear's margin drag (cost pass-through lag) is flagged by management as normalising in coming quarters.
negative_para: [DATA] Lloyd remains the known profitability drag and least predictable segment: -6.5% YoY in Q3 FY26 and -19% YoY in Q4 FY26 (delayed seasonality cited both times) before recovering in Q1 FY27 - two bad prints out of the last three is a real pattern, not noise - and the segment is exposed to intensifying competition from Voltas and Korean/Chinese AC brands (LG, Samsung, Daikin, Blue Star premium). [DATA] Switchgear revenue fell in Q1 FY27 (Rs.607.68cr) on West-Asia-linked export disruption on top of Q4 FY26's cost-pass-through-lag margin hit - two consecutive quarters of segment softness for different reasons. [DATA] Consolidated EBITDA margin has now compressed in back-to-back prints: Q4 FY26 to 10.9% from 11.6% YoY, and Q1 FY27 EBITDA (ex other income) down 9.6% YoY even as revenue grew 19% - operating leverage is currently negative. [OPINION] Valuation is rich: TTM PE ~40-43x and analyst consensus target ~Rs.1,443-1,497 already prices continued double-digit-plus earnings compounding; a reverse DCF at this multiple embeds an aggressive long-run growth assumption the FY26/Q1FY27 core (ex the Goldi Solar one-off) has not yet delivered, leaving little cushion if Lloyd or switchgear disappoint again.
reverse_dcf_judgment: [INFERENCE] Rich. Stock ~Rs.1,187-1,200 (17-20 Jul 26), market cap ~Rs.74,500cr, TTM PE ~40-43x (range across trackers). Back-solving a 40x+ multiple for a consumer-durables business with a cyclical AC arm implies the market is pricing sustained mid-to-high-teens EPS compounding for an extended runway. FY26 core PAT growth (ex the Rs.283cr Goldi Solar FV one-off) is closer to flat-to-high-single-digit given Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell 3.6% YoY, and Q1 FY27 core (EBITDA ex other income) fell 9.6% YoY (PAT -16.6%) on deliberate A&P investment. Current delivered core growth is running below what the multiple embeds - cables' strength (+20-27%) is doing the heavy lifting while Lloyd/switchgear volatility offsets it at the margin line. Not an absurd multiple (consumer-electricals peers Crompton/Voltas also trade rich on brand-quality narratives), but not cheap or fair either - no margin of safety priced in.
